designationHistory.name: Blackwater Migratory Bird Refuge
designationHistory.indexText: Blackwater Migratory Bird Refuge was established under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act as a sanctuary for waterfowl on the Atlantic Flyway.
designationHistory.note: The refuge page gives only the month or year. The refuge page does not say how it was established.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge, About Us
Friends of Blackwater NWR, History of the Refuge: "established in 1933 as a refuge for migratory birds"
American Presidency Project: Proclamation 2416, Changing the Names of Certain Federal Wildlife Refuges (July 25, 1940), lists former and new names

review.note: 1933 per Friends group and FWS; a 1991 refuge annual narrative says 1932, so the exact date (MBCC approval vs. first purchase) is still open. Former name per Proclamation 2416.

designationHistory.indexOriginal: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge (NWR) was established in 1933 as a waterfowl sanctuary for birds migrating along the Atlantic Flyway, and currently encompasses more than 32,000 acres.
